Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.tuner

Class Tuning

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.tuner.Tuning
public final class Tuning extends Object
A named instrument tuning: an ordered set of target notes (low string to high) with the equal-tempered reference frequency of each, plus the search that maps a detected pitch to the nearest string and its deviation in cents.

The built-in tunings cover the common guitar and bass sets, but a tuning is just a name and an ordered list of string MIDI numbers, so any custom set can be built with of(String, int...) (e.g. Drop C = C2 G2 C3 F3 A3 D4 = Tuning.of("Guitar (Drop C)", 36, 43, 48, 53, 57, 62)). User-defined tunings are persisted by TuningStore and offered alongside the built-ins. A CHROMATIC tuning has no target strings and simply reports the nearest note, which is the right mode for tuning by ear or for other instruments.

Like Note, everything here is pure java.lang.Math - no AWT, no audio device - so the whole tuning table and its nearest-string search are unit-testable headless. String MIDI numbers use the same reference as Note (A4 = MIDI 69 = 440.0f Hz).

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static Tuning of(String name, int... midi)
      Builds a custom tuning from the MIDI numbers of its strings, low to high. This is the public factory the tuner's "add tuning" UI and the persisted store use; it is exactly equivalent to the constructor and exists so a caller can name the intent (e.g. Tuning.of("Guitar (Drop C)", 36, 43, 48, 53, 57, 62)).
      Parameters:
      name - the human-readable tuning name
      midi - the string MIDI numbers, low to high (empty for chromatic)
      Returns:
      the new tuning
